answer: Persistent Loss Ledger: each identity accrues a non-transferable history score; new identities start below a viability threshold and only earn standing by completing work over a long horizon. Cloning resets that history, so every clone pays the full ramp-up cost again while splitting revenue. An attacker's marginal clone therefore loses money: it absorbs setup cost and forgone earnings yet cannot pool reputation. Enforce with a karst-like uneven entry gradient—early tasks pay little, later ones pay more—so the payoff stays crystal clear: clones cost more than they earn.
